_doc: Machine-readable index of open, batch-addressable backlog items for the Routine's systemic-fix mode (prompts/routine2.md §B). The wiki-maintenance session keeps this in sync with the prose backlog pages (ideas/cleanup-backlog.md, ideas/tooling-backlog.md). The selector (pipeline/routine_next.py) picks the lowest-'priority'-number item with status=='open' AND batch_ready==true. EVERY fix is verified per-entry before changing anything (the detectors are read-only review queues); 'fix_type' only indicates how safe the transform is once verified.

items.title: Furigana wrappers with truncated readings (visibly wrong on the live site)
items.filter: subpattern == 'reading-truncated' (do these first), then 'pure-kana' reversed and 'nested'
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-09: Fixed 74 reading-truncated entries (e.g. {やり方|かた}→やり{方|かた}), 9 pure-kana reversed, and 7 nested brace patterns. 130 slash-reading entries remain under the separate furigana-slash-reading item (priority 4).

items.title: {ている} furigana-brace artifact in notes/examples
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-10: All 49 entries fixed ({ている} → plain ている in the ASPECT (...) section headers). Each entry opened and confirmed per-entry before saving; furigana self-check screened the 49 changed IDs (5 flags, all rejected as partial-reading false positives, none related to the edit). Detector now reports 0. Brace syntax {X|Y} is for kanji+reading only; {ている} is pure kana so the removal drops no reading.

items.title: [Register: ...] legacy trailer in notes
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-10: All 188 entries fixed. Per-entry verification confirmed all formality fields already carried the equivalent register information (formality field has no 'polite' value — 'neutral' is correct; 'casual' in the trailer maps to 'informal' in the schema). Furigana self-check screened all 188 changed IDs: 5 flags, all rejected as pre-existing false positives unrelated to the edit (rendaku misread, data-extraction artifact, cross-ref without furigana in unrelated notes). Detector now reports 0.

items.title: Dual-reading furigana with slash separators
items.notes: {村|むら/そん} style is non-standard and misrenders. Pick the correct single reading for the context; mention the alternate reading in notes if useful.

items.title: cross_references / prominent_see_also entries without a target_id
items.notes: A dangling reference object lacks target_id. Resolve the intended entry id (build/word_id_lookup.json), or drop the reference if no entry exists.

items.title: Conjugation field on a non-verb / non-i-adjective entry
items.notes: Mostly resolved (P6) and guarded against regeneration; kept as a standing check. If any appear, confirm POS, then strip the spurious conjugation field and stray verb_class tag.

items.title: politeness=humble/honorific with no supporting notes
items.notes: Distinguish true keigo from uchi/soto reference forms and bikago. Fix the tag or add the explanation; do not bulk-retag.

items.title: Non-standard but mostly-rendering furigana wrappers (o/go-prefix, pure-kana, over-wrapped okurigana)
items.notes: Mostly cosmetic (canonical form: お{酒|さけ}, {若|わか}い). Lower priority. Verify each rewrap against build/word_id_lookup.json so inline-link lookups still resolve.

items.title: semantic == ['general'] (under-specified)
items.notes: Low-urgency enrichment, not an error. Only replace 'general' when a specific tag clearly applies from the gloss; otherwise leave it. Large scope — drain slowly.

items.title: formality=formal over-applied to neutral/everyday words in early entries (P17)
items.detect: python3 -c "import json,glob; [print(d['id']) for p in glob.glob('entries/*/*.json') for d in [json.load(open(p))] if (d.get('metadata',{}).get('tags',{}).get('formality')=='formal') and (int(d['id'])<500)]"
items.notes: batch_ready:false — the accuracy-review mode's formality-dimension pass is the right instrument (cross-model signal helps distinguish genuinely formal vocabulary from over-tagged neutrals). The accuracy-review frontier is currently fixing these as it advances through the 00001–00500 range; confirmed range through 00450. Once accuracy-review passes 00500, reassess if a standalone systemic-fix batch is warranted.

items.title: 'descriptive' semantic tag as catch-all on non-mimetic words (P18)
items.detect: python3 -c "import json,glob; [print(d['id']) for p in glob.glob('entries/*/*.json') for d in [json.load(open(p))] if d.get('metadata',{}).get('tags',{}).get('semantic')==['descriptive'] and d.get('metadata',{}).get('tags',{}).get('pos',[''])[0] in ('noun','adjective-na','adverb','conjunction','expression')]"
items.notes: batch_ready:false — fold into the accuracy-review tags pass rather than a dedicated sweep. When reviewing, replace a stray 'descriptive' on an abstract/grammatical word with the right domain tag, or drop it in favour of 'general'. Reserve 'descriptive' for mimetics and manner-quality words. See topics/schema-tag-reliability.md → Undefined tag semantics.

items.title: Concrete semantic tag with no keyword match in the gloss (batch tag drift, P11)
items.notes: P11 is the most pervasive tag-drift problem. The AUTHORITATIVE path is now the accuracy-review mode's LLM tag pass (build/review_accuracy.py --dimensions tags), which judges each semantic tag against the headword (not example topics) and is validated to flag e.g. body-part on 切り捨てる. This keyword detector (check_tag_drift.py --check semantic-mismatch) stays batch_ready:false / experimental — it is a free, noisy manual-audit aid only (flags boat=transportation, school=building). Do NOT drive systemic-fix from it.

items.title: Noun examples that never contain their headword (misparses, wrong-word examples)
items.notes: Two tiers: 'reading-only' (14 — kana reading present without the kanji form; either a cross-boundary misparse like 仕様 inside 直しようがない, or legitimate kana orthography like ごちそう — judge per entry) and 'headword-absent' (129 — example may show a related compound, a verb form of the nominal, or simply the wrong word, e.g. 目玉焼き in the 卵 entry). Replace bad examples with genuine headword examples carrying full inline links, or remove if the entry has examples to spare. Motivating case 00472 仕様 fixed 2026-06-10 (curator-directed).

items.title: Out-of-taxonomy semantic tags (post-expansion migration)
items.filter: records whose detail contains 'suggested:' first (1:1 near-duplicate migrations, ~2060 instances), then the long tail
items.notes: Curator tag-policy decision 2026-06-11: VALID_SEMANTIC expanded with 30 established tags (>=100 uses); remaining 9,036 instances across 7,292 entries migrate to in-list tags. Near-duplicates carry suggested targets (TAG_MIGRATION map in check_tag_drift.py) but still verify per entry. accuracy-review prompt v3 also drains this organically. See topics/schema-tag-reliability.md.
